packageRules.description: @eks-agent/pricing dep refresh — fast pickup on its small dep surface (@eks-agent/core via workspace:* + the standard devDeps). The PRICES table itself is NOT Renovate-managed; scripts/refresh-pricing.mjs (Phase 2) handles that via a separate AWS Pricing API workflow on its own cron schedule. The accelerated schedule here is for the package.json deps, not the PRICES content.

The eval-runner image's kubectl and AWS CLI travel in their own PR rather than the all-non-major group. Each bump lands with the image's per-architecture checksums still naming the previous release, so the eval-runner image job fails on sha256sum until they are refreshed, and that failure has to hold back only this PR.

kubectl in the eval-runner image stays on the minor of the org's EKS cluster version target (landing-zone's cluster_version default), whose ±1 version-skew window also covers clusters one minor either side of it. Renovate proposes that minor's patches and nothing outside it. Moving the minor follows a change of the cluster version target, and is made in the same change that moves this range.

customManagers.description: Tool versions pinned as workflow env vars. Renovate parses `uses:` refs natively but not a version a step installs itself, so without these the scanners deciding whether this repo is clean would age silently — and the one that ages worst is the security tooling, where a stale rule set reads as a clean tree. scripts/check-version-pins.py asserts every such pin is matched here.
zizmor, installed from PyPI by the workflow static-analysis job.
PyYAML, installed from PyPI at a workflow- or job-level version by every job that runs a gate parsing YAML.
govulncheck, installed with `go install` by the security workflow.
tflint, pinned as a setup-tflint action input rather than a `uses:` ref.
OpenTofu, pinned as a setup-opentofu action input.

golangci-lint. Pinned as a job-level env var rather than inline on the action input, so one discovery pattern covers every tool version in the repo — scripts/check-version-pins.py finds NAME_VERSION and nothing else.

The Anthropic `ant` CLI the sandbox worker runs. Its two per-architecture checksums are deliberately NOT auto-bumped: a digest Renovate could rewrite unread is a supply-chain check that verifies nothing. A version bump lands with stale checksums, the image build fails on sha256sum, and the failure is the prompt to refresh them from the upstream checksums file.

kubectl in the eval-runner image. Its two per-architecture checksums are not auto-bumped, for the reason the ant entry above states; the eval-runner image job in ci.yaml builds both platforms, so the stale-checksum failure surfaces on the Renovate PR itself.

The AWS CLI v2 in the eval-runner image. Each v2 version is a git tag on aws/aws-cli with no GitHub release behind it, hence github-tags. Its checksums are refreshed by hand on the same terms as kubectl's.

The Kubernetes version envtest runs the conformance suite against. It is the API server the CEL validation rules in four CRDs are actually exercised on, so it ageing is a silent loss of coverage rather than a stale dependency.

promtool. The SLO assertions execute real PromQL against synthetic series through this binary, so its version decides what those tests actually prove — a pin ageing here is a silent change in the semantics being asserted, not a stale convenience.

cosign, pinned as the cosign-installer `cosign-release` input. The release decides the signature format the release workflow writes, and the cluster verify-images policy reads that format, so it moves through a reviewed bump rather than with the installer's default.
A tool release passed as an action's `version` input, named by the `# renovate:` comment above it. Read in the workflows and in the composite actions under .github/actions/ they call.
